name: Input Capture
description: Adversaries may use methods of capturing user input to obtain credentials or collect information. During normal device usage, users often provide credentials to various locations, such as login pages/portals or system dialog boxes. Input capture mechanisms may be transparent to the user (e.g. [Keylogging](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1417/001)) or rely on deceiving the user into providing input into what they believe to be a genuine application prompt (e.g. [GUI Input Capture](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1417/002)).

telemetry.name: Application Log Content
telemetry.description: Application-emitted audit or operational event content.
telemetry.collection_focus: Select the application event family required by the detection and document its native schema before normalization.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

telemetry.name: File Creation
telemetry.description: Creation or overwrite of a file at an observed path.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope Sysmon FileCreate (11) to the lab directory; retain the process and file path. Differentiate creation/overwrite if the sensor can.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

analytics.name: Analytic 1825
analytics.guidance: Defender observes an app gaining input-observation capability (AccessibilityService enablement, default IME set, draw-over-apps permission), then creating an intercept surface (overlay window, accessibility event stream consumption or IME keystroke callbacks), followed by persistence (local keylog/clipboard dump) and/or small, frequent network egress. Chain: capability/permission → listener/overlay activation → bursty input read events → local write → near-term exfil.

tuning.description: Max time from input intercept to persist/exfil (e.g., 5–45s).
Minimum count of input events within window to flag harvesting (e.g., ≥5).
Require overlay creation if Accessibility not present (true/false).
Regex for keylog/clipboard dump destinations in app container.
Known-good analytics/CDN endpoints to suppress FPs.
Foreground/background/Work Profile or Kiosk policy to scope alerts.

log_sources.name: android:logcat
log_sources.channel: Grant/activation of BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, BIND_INPUT_METHOD, SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, POST_NOTIFICATIONS for <pkg>

log_sources.name: android:logcat
log_sources.channel: Default IME changed/active: imeId=<pkg>, onStartInput/onFinishInput high frequency. TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY|addView .* showing on top of package <otherPkg>

analytics.name: Analytic 1826
analytics.guidance: Defender observes an app enabling or using input-capture surfaces (custom keyboard extension with Full Access, abnormal UI text entry interception, pasteboard polling adjacent to login screens), then persisting and/or exfiltrating captured input. Chain: capability/consent (TCC for keyboard Full Access or input privacy domains) → intercept behavior (keyboard extension active, repeated text field ‘editingChanged’/secure entry focus, background pasteboard reads) → local write → near-term egress.

tuning.description: Max time from intercept to persist/exfil (e.g., 5–60s).
Minimum key/commit or editingChanged count to flag harvesting (e.g., ≥10).
Require keyboard Full Access to escalate severity (true/false).
Foreground state, Focus modes, MDM policy.

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Keyboard extension Full Access change; privacy grant touching input/keyboard categories for <bundle_id>

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: UIWindow/UIView events indicating secure text entry focus, editingChanged bursts, unexpected firstResponder cycling

log_sources.name: iOS:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: CREATE/WRITE clipboard/keylog artifacts (clipboard.db, keys_*.txt) in container

software.name: Phenakite
software.description: [Phenakite](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1126) has used phishing sites for iCloud and Facebook if either of those were used for authentication during the chat sign up process.(Citation: fb_arid_viper)

references.description: Flossman, M., Scott, M. (2021, April). Technical Paper // Taking Action Against Arid Viper. Retrieved November 17, 2024.

software.name: CherryBlos
software.description: [CherryBlos](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1225) has captured victims' credentials through predefined fake activities.(Citation: TrendMicro_CherryBlos_July2023)

references.description: Trend Micro Research. (2023, July 28). Related CherryBlos and FakeTrade Android Malware Involved in Scam Campaigns. Retrieved March 28, 2025.

software.name: GodFather
software.description: [GodFather](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1231) has the captured information about the device's screen to include detailed tap events.(Citation: ZimperiumOrtegaPratapagiri_GodFather_Jun2025)

references.description: Ortega, F. Pratapagiri, V. (2025, June 18). Your Mobile App, Their Playground: The Dark Side of Virtualization. Retrieved July 16, 2025.

mitigations.name: Use Recent OS Version
mitigations.description: The `HIDE_OVERLAY_WINDOWS` permission was introduced in Android 12 allowing apps to hide overlay windows of type `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` drawn by other apps with the `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` permission, preventing other applications from creating overlay windows on top of the current application.(Citation: Android 12 Features)

references.description: Google. (2022, April 4). Features and APIs Overview. Retrieved April 5, 2022.

mitigations.name: User Guidance
mitigations.description: Users should be wary of granting applications dangerous or privacy-intrusive permissions, such as keyboard registration or accessibility service access.

mitigations.name: Enterprise Policy
mitigations.description: When using Samsung Knox, third-party keyboards must be explicitly added to an allow list in order to be available to the end-user.(Citation: Samsung Keyboards) An EMM/MDM can use the Android `DevicePolicyManager.setPermittedAccessibilityServices` method to set an explicit list of applications that are allowed to use Android's accessibility features.

references.description: Samsung. (2019, August 16). 3rd party keyboards must be whitelisted.. Retrieved November 17, 2024.

simulation.prerequisites: Use owned test devices or emulators, disposable app accounts and test data. Verify platform/version instrumentation; desktop test procedures do not establish mobile coverage.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
